## Higher-order semantic reconstruction

7 October 2026. [Ren asks to finish the higher-order milestone](../../../sources/15-codex-theory-conversations/2026-10-07-finish-higher-order-reconstruction.md). [The checked integration](../../../_process/research/2026-10-05-generative-foundation-review/root-foundation/ROOT-MATHEMATICAL-HIGHER-ORDER-INTEGRATION.md) now completes the conditional semantic connection. The existing correspondence between predicates and finite-subset ideals is extended to actual higher-order syntax and all-formula truth preservation. A fresh Lean 4.29.1 build passes 43 new named theorems and 97 declaration audits, with only the reported standard dependencies.

The first module covers full relational second-order semantics at every finite arity, including mixed individual/relation quantifiers, relation application and extensional predicate equality. The second recursively interprets finite types built from a supplied base, predicate types and full function types. At every predicate layer it constructs the concrete ideal-completion correspondence; at function types it transports the full function by the argument/result bijections. Lambda/application evaluation, equality, membership and quantification at every represented type preserve meaning. Truth preservation is proved from these constructed maps, not supplied as their defining condition.

This reaches predicates of predicates and functions between higher types. The finite-type grammar has no internal universe, dependent types or distinguished truth-value term type. A checked semantic comprehension theorem gives each formula-defined extension an ideal presentation; no effective truth procedure or formula-to-term comprehension constructor is asserted. The supplied base bijection may be the identity.

The fullness commitment remains visible. Corresponding selected predicate/ideal ranges are full together. On the same natural-number domain, the sentence “there exists a predicate holding of every element” is true under full quantification and false under finite-only predicate quantification. This tests an actual change of range; the restricted family is not claimed to satisfy Henkin comprehension. It does not show that every proper restriction changes some sentence, or refute a root that admits full completion.

**Strongest new claim:** under the specified full-domain commitments, recursive predicate completion and function transport preserve every formula of the declared higher-order languages. This semantic milestone is complete. The next universal derivation must justify full predicate/function admission and establish the proposed constitutive dependence; placing those resources within the whole does not alone explain their necessity. Earlier completion-attempt conclusions below remain valid for that stronger target.
